headline: Huawei, Cambricon and other Chinese AI chipmakers have raised prices by roughly 20% to 50% as a memory shortage lifts their costs, sources say.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: concrete price rises across several firms, though they rest on unnamed sources.
importance_line: Higher prices raise the cost of building AI computing in China and show the memory shortage and US export limits squeezing Beijing's push to replace Nvidia, but the figures come from unnamed sources and the companies did not comment.
summary: The Standard (Hong Kong) reports, citing three people familiar with the matter, that Huawei has raised the indicated price of its Ascend 950DT AI accelerator card to above 250,000 yuan, 20% to 50% more than quoted two months ago, while Cambricon's next chip is priced 20% to 30% higher and smaller rivals MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX made similar rises. The sources link the increases to a worldwide shortage of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory chips central to AI processors, which Chinese firms increasingly buy through grey-market channels at several times the usual price since US export controls tightened in December 2024.
notes: The Standard's text reads like a wire report but does not name another outlet, so The Standard is credited. Companies did not respond to requests for comment. Search found no other outlet carrying it.
